Wisdom (Biblical)
WIZ-duhm
noun (gift and grace)
From Old English wisdom, the quality of being wise; rendering Hebrew chokmah and Greek sophia, the skill of living rightly before God.

📖 Biblical Definition

Wisdom in Scripture is not bare knowledge nor worldly cleverness, but the God-given skill of ordering all of life in the fear of the LORD. Its beginning and first principle is reverence toward God: "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge" (Prov 1:7), and again, "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding" (Prov 9:10). Hebrew chokmah denotes a practical mastery, the craftsman's skill applied to the whole craft of godly living, so that the wise man walks in the paths of righteousness and shuns the way of the fool. This wisdom is finally a Person, for Christ "of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption" (1 Cor 1:30); to have Him is to have wisdom itself, and the cross which the world calls foolishness is the very wisdom of God. The wisdom from above is also a moral character: "first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be intreated" (Jas 3:17). This dictionary confesses that true wisdom is not the boast of the learned nor the shrewdness of the worldly, but the fear of God worked by His Spirit, found and treasured in Christ, and shown forth in a holy and useful life.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Wisdom is the God-given skill of living rightly, beginning in the fear of the LORD. It is found supremely in Christ, who is made unto us wisdom. It is practical godliness, not mere intellect or worldly cleverness.

expand to see more

WISDOM, noun. The God-given skill of ordering one's life and affairs rightly in the fear of the LORD.

It is distinguished from mere knowledge, cleverness, or the wisdom of this world, which God brings to nought.

"The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding" (Prov 9:10).

It requires reverence, obedience, and the choosing of righteousness; it forbids the folly that despises instruction.

Its fulness and treasury is Christ, who is made unto us wisdom from God.

📖 Key Scripture

Prov 1:7 — "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction."

Prov 9:10 — "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding."

1 Cor 1:30 — "But of him are ye in Christ Jesus, who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption."

Jas 3:17 — "But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be intreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The age severs wisdom from the fear of God, making it a self-derived cleverness, technique, or inner intuition rather than reverent, obedient skill in living.

expand to see more

The world prizes a wisdom that begins not in the fear of God but in self, whether the academic shrewdness of the learned or the soft "inner wisdom" of the therapeutic age that tells men to trust their hearts. But Scripture calls the heart deceitful, and the wisdom of this world foolishness with God. To divorce wisdom from reverence is to build skill upon sand, however polished the result may appear.

Recover the biblical order: the fear of the LORD first, then knowledge, then a life skillfully built in righteousness. Such wisdom is humble, teachable, and finally Christological, for all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hid in Christ. The believer grows wise not by climbing into himself but by bowing before God and feeding on His word.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Wisdom renders Hebrew chokmah, skill, and Greek sophia, both anchored in the fear of the LORD.

expand to see more

Hebrew chokmah first describes the skill of artisans (Exod 31:3) before naming the skill of godly living.

Greek sophia in 1 Cor 1:30 is fulfilled in Christ, in whom wisdom is incarnate.

The recurring formula "the fear of the LORD" (Prov 1:7; 9:10) names wisdom's beginning and principle.

Old English wisdom joins wis, wise, to the suffix denoting state or quality.

James 3:17 supplies the moral marks of the wisdom from above, pure and peaceable.

Usage

"He sought wisdom not in cleverness but in the fear of the LORD, where Scripture says it begins."

"True wisdom is found in Christ, who of God is made unto us wisdom and righteousness."

"The young man mistook worldly cleverness for wisdom and stumbled into the way of the fool."
